title: Dulia/hyperdulia names lack conciliar sanction; Pérez dislikes ‘dulia’ as implying servitude to fellow-servants
source_text: IV. Porro, quanquam Theologi Ecclesiae Romanae, cultum Beatae Virginis & Sanctorum proprium, communiter Duliam & Hyperduliam vocent, ut a caeteris cultus speciebus distinguant, iste tamen vocis Duliae & Hyperduliae usus, nondum est authoritate publica Conciliorum in Ecclesia Romana sancitus atque definitus. Ac propterea Martinus Pereziius Episcopus Hispanus, in suo opere de traditionibus, referente Bellarmino, testatur sibi non multum probari nomen Duliae sumptum pro cultu Sanctorum, cum Dulia proprie significet servitutem, & nos non simus servi Sanctorum, sed conservi.
pass_a_gloss: Further, although the Theologians of the Roman Church commonly call the proper cult of the Blessed Virgin and of the Saints Dulia and Hyperdulia, that they may distinguish it from the other species of cult, yet that use of the word Dulia and Hyperdulia is not yet sanctioned and defined by the public authority of Councils in the Roman Church. And therefore Martin Pérez, a Spanish Bishop, in his work on traditions, Bellarmine reporting, testifies that the name Dulia taken for the cult of the Saints does not much please him, since Dulia properly signifies servitude, and we are not servants of the Saints, but fellow-servants.
pass_b_english: School use of dulia/hyperdulia is not yet fixed by Roman Councils.
Pérez (via Bellarmino) dislikes calling saint-cult ‘dulia,’ since the word means servitude and we are conservi, not their slaves.

lemmas.gloss: is not yet by public authority of Councils

choices.why: Pérez’s objection: Saints are co-servants under God.
